question: Last year Neil bought two watches. This year he sold them for ₹15,000 each. On one, he made a 25% profit and on the other, he had a x% loss. If his net loss is ₹2000, then find the value of x.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Selling Price (SP) = 15,000 × 2 = ₹30,000.

Total Cost Price (CP) = Total SP + Net Loss = 30,000 + 2000 = ₹32,000.

CP of 1st watch (sold at 25% profit) = 15,000 × (100 ÷ 125) = ₹12,000.

CP of 2nd watch = 32,000 − 12,000 = ₹20,000.

Loss% on 2nd watch = [(20,000 − 15,000) ÷ 20,000] × 100 = 25%.

**∴ The correct answer is 25%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Selling price of each watch = ₹15,000

Profit on 1st watch = 25%

Net overall loss = ₹2000

Loss on 2nd watch = x%

**Formula Used:**

Cost Price (CP) = (SP × 100) ÷ (100 + Profit%)

Loss% = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100
